mainTopic: Giving up rights (ביטול רשות): when it can be undone, and whether a מומר or צדוקי can do it
overview: The גמרא asks whether someone who gave up his rights in a shared alleyway (ביטול רשות) can take them back by carrying there. רבי מאיר seems to contradict himself on this point. רב יוסף fixes the text to solve the contradiction. אביי instead says it depends on whether the other residents already took possession (החזיקו) of the alleyway, and a ברייתא backs him up. Next, the גמרא compares two versions of רבי יהודה's report about the צדוקי neighbor. The ברייתא's version suggests that the צדוקי is like a גוי, but the משנה's version suggests that his giving up of rights works. The answer is that a מומר who breaks שבת in private can give up his rights, while one who breaks שבת in public is like a גוי. A story about a man who hid his ring from רבי יהודה נשיאה shows this rule in action. Finally, רב הונא defines a מומר as one who breaks שבת in public, and רב נחמן challenges this definition. His challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A contradiction from another משנה in רבי מאיר's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר says that a person who renounced his rights and then carried makes carrying forbidden again. This seems to contradict רבי מאיר's view in the משנה about the צדוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: Someone who gave away his rights and then carried something out, whether by accident or on purpose, makes carrying forbidden for everyone. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. It brings another משנה where רבי מאיר seems to hold the opposite of what he held about the צדוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the צדוקי case, once a resident renounces his rights, his later carrying does not take them back. Here, רבי מאיר says that carrying after renouncing does take them back and forbids everyone, even if he carried by accident. So רבי מאיר seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? (formula that opens a challenge)
Gave away his rights, i.e., renounced his share in the shared area (ביטול רשות)
By accident, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
He makes carrying forbidden for everyone else

steps.confusionAlert: 'אוסר' here does not mean he is personally punished. It means his carrying cancels his renunciation, so his rights are back in the shared area and nobody may carry there.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: one who gave away his rights
phrases.notes: He renounced his share because he forgot to join the עירוב.

phrases.english: and then carried out, whether by accident or on purpose,
he makes it forbidden. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading of the צדוקי משנה (on the previous amud) by citing a conflicting statement of רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's position, implied in the צדוקי משנה, that a renunciation cannot be undone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה has רבי מאיר saying that carrying after renouncing does undo it and forbids everyone, so he contradicts himself.

steps.title: רב יוסף changes the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף fixes the contradiction by changing the text: the משנה should say 'he does not make it forbidden.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Change the wording to read 'he does not make it forbidden.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by correcting the text of the second משנה so it matches the צדוקי case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the difference between the two sources, רב יוסף says the second one was written wrong. With his correction, רבי מאיר holds in both places that carrying after renouncing does not take the rights back.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (introduces a change to the text)
He does not make it forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Say instead: "He does not make it forbidden."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is fixing the wording of the משנה it just quoted, so read it this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says רבי מאיר holds the person makes it forbidden, which contradicts the צדוקי case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading is 'אינו אוסר', so רבי מאיר is consistent.

steps.title: אביי: it depends on whether the residents already took possession
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the text as it is. He says the two sources speak about different cases: in one the residents already took possession of the alleyway, and in the other they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. Here, the residents of the alleyway already took possession of it. There, the residents of the alleyway did not take possession of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer that does not change any text. He splits the two sources into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the other residents already took possession (החזיקו) of the alleyway, for example by bringing their things out, the renunciation is locked in and his later carrying cannot undo it. That is the צדוקי case. If they had not yet taken possession, his carrying does take his rights back and forbids everyone. That is the משנה where רבי מאיר says 'אוסר'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer that splits the cases)
Here... there (each source refers to a different case)
They took possession of the area
The residents of the alleyway

steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's distinction becomes the key rule: a renunciation becomes final once the others have taken possession.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
here, where the residents of the alleyway had taken possession of the alleyway,
phrases.notes: This is the צדוקי's case: once they've taken over the alleyway, he can't take back what he gave up.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְזִיקוּ בְּנֵי מָבוֹי בַּמָּבוֹי.
phrases.english: there, where the residents of the alleyway had not taken possession of the alleyway.
phrases.notes: This is the case where his carrying cancels what he gave up, so he is אוסר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב יוסף's, without changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements of רבי מאיר speak about the same case and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They speak about different cases: whether or not the residents had already taken possession.

steps.title: A ברייתא: carrying before renouncing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports אביי. Its first part deals with someone who carried before he renounced his rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught in a ברייתא: If he carried before he gave away his rights, whether by accident or on purpose, he can still renounce. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: If he carried by accident, he can renounce. If he carried on purpose, he cannot renounce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that will support אביי. This first part sets the stage and is not yet the proof itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part covers a person who carried before renouncing. רבי מאיר lets him renounce afterward in any case. רבי יהודה says that if he broke the rule on purpose, he loses the ability to renounce. The key line for אביי comes at the end of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא (here it brings support)
Before
To renounce (his rights)
רבי יהודה, who disagrees with רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: 'והתניא' usually opens a challenge, but here it brings support for אביי. Its job is to back up the answer, not attack it.

phrases.english: And it was taught: before he gave away his rights,
if he carried out, whether by accident or on purpose,
he can renounce. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּשׁוֹגֵג יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: by accident, he can renounce;
on purpose, he cannot renounce.
phrases.notes: Someone who breaks שבת on purpose is treated like a non-Jew, who cannot renounce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a ברייתא brought to support אביי.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's distinction between 'took possession' and 'did not take possession'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: carrying after renouncing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now deals with someone who carried after he renounced. רבי מאיר says he makes it forbidden either way. רבי יהודה says only if he did it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who gave away his rights and then carried out, whether by accident or on purpose, makes it forbidden. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: On purpose, he makes it forbidden. By accident, he does not make it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the case of carrying after renouncing. It repeats the same wording as the משנה from step 1, and it is still setting up the key line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the original text, 'אוסר', in רבי מאיר's name. That fits אביי, who kept the text, and not רב יוסף, who changed it. רבי יהודה says an accidental act does not cancel the renunciation, but a deliberate act does.

keyTerms.meaning: And he carried out (from his house into the shared area)
The words of (marks whose view it is)

phrases.english: One who gave away his rights and then carried out,
whether by accident or on purpose, makes it forbidden;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: on purpose, he makes it forbidden;
by accident, he does not make it forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the second case, after renouncing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After renouncing, רבי מאיר says carrying always forbids. רבי יהודה says only deliberate carrying forbids.

steps.title: The ברייתא's limit: once they took possession, no one forbids
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its ruling to a case where the residents had not taken possession. If they had, everyone agrees he does not make it forbidden. This is exactly אביי's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When the residents of the alleyway had not taken possession of the alleyway. But if the residents of the alleyway had taken possession of it, whether by accident or on purpose, he does not make it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual proof. The ברייתא itself makes the same distinction אביי made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'במה דברים אמורים' limit the earlier ruling to a case where the residents did not take possession. Once they did take possession, even רבי מאיר agrees that carrying cannot undo the renunciation. This settles the contradiction just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this apply? (introduces a limit on the ruling)
But
In the alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: A renunciation (ביטול רשות) can be undone by carrying only if the other residents have not yet taken possession. Once they took possession, it is final for everyone. This matches אביי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא supports אביי over רב יוסף's change to the text, and it sets the point at which a renunciation becomes final.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where the residents of the alleyway had not taken possession of the alleyway;
but if the residents of the alleyway had taken possession of the alleyway,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג וּבֵין בְּמֵזִיד — אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר.
phrases.english: whether by accident or on purpose, he does not make it forbidden.
phrases.notes: Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agree in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the limiting clause that proves אביי's answer.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's answer: whether the residents took possession decides whether he can be אוסר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own limiting clause (במה דברים אמורים)
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once the residents have taken possession, the renouncer's carrying never forbids, by accident or on purpose.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's version and drawing an inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: רבי יהודה says רבן גמליאל told them to hurry and use the alleyway before nightfall. From this the גמרא infers that the צדוקי is treated like a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says it in different words: 'Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway before it gets dark, and he will forbid it for you.' This shows that he is treated like a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ברייתא quoted earlier and draws a conclusion from its wording. This sets up the next step, where the conclusion will clash with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deadline is nightfall. That means once שבת starts, the צדוקי forbids the alleyway no matter what he does. So giving up his rights would not help, and that is exactly the law for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' This is how the גמרא quotes a source it mentioned earlier, in order to discuss it.
In different words, meaning a different version of the same story.
Before it gets dark, meaning before שבת begins.
'This shows that.' It introduces a conclusion drawn from the wording of a source.
A non-Jew. A גוי cannot give up his rights in an alleyway. His rights must be rented instead.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֶרֶת:
phrases.english: The Master said: Rabbi Yehuda says in a different formulation:
Hurry and do your needs in the alleyway
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל's words about the צדוקי neighbor.

phrases.english: before it gets dark and he forbids it for you.
Apparently, he is considered a gentile.
phrases.notes: His renunciation does not help, just like a גוי's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of carrying after renouncing and returns to an earlier ברייתא to analyze its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא's version of רבי יהודה, a צדוקי is like a גוי, and his giving up of rights does not work.

steps.title: The משנה's wording points the other way
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבי יהודה's version says 'before he takes out his things.' That implies the צדוקי's giving up of rights does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'before he takes out'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference by pointing to the משנה. There, the deadline is 'before he takes out his things,' not 'before dark.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the danger only begins when the צדוקי takes his things out, then until then his giving up of rights still counts. That means he is not like a גוי. So two sources quoting רבי יהודה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely.' It opens a challenge.
'We learned' in a משנה.
Before he takes out his belongings into the alleyway.

phrases.english: But we learned in the mishna: 'before he takes out'!
phrases.notes: This implies his renunciation works until he actually takes things out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of Step 7 using the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יהודה treats the צדוקי like a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's version of רבי יהודה makes the deadline his taking things out. That implies his giving up of rights is valid, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: First answer: read the משנה as 'before the day goes out'
steps.stepSummary: Change the reading of the משנה to 'עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא הַיּוֹם', meaning before the day ends. Then it matches the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it reads: 'before the day goes out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adding one word to the משנה. With that word, 'יוציא' refers to the day ending, not to the צדוקי taking out his things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added word, the משנה also gives nightfall as the deadline. Now both sources agree that the צדוקי is like a גוי. The contradiction is gone because the משנה's text is fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say.' Here it means: read the text this way.
The day goes out, meaning Friday ends.

phrases.english: Say: 'before the day goes out.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'יוציא' meant the צדוקי taking out his things, which would make his giving up of rights valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יוציא' refers to the day ending. Both sources set nightfall as the deadline, so he is like a גוי.

steps.title: Second answer: breaking שבת in private versus in public
steps.stepSummary: Keep the משנה's text as it is. The משנה speaks about a מומר who breaks שבת in private, and his giving up of rights works. The ברייתא speaks about one who breaks שבת in public, and he is like a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say there is no difficulty. Here it is a מומר who breaks שבת in private. There it is a מומר who breaks שבת in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer that does not change any words. It explains that the two sources are talking about two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who breaks שבת secretly is still treated as a Jew, so he can give up his rights. That is the case of the משנה. Someone who breaks שבת openly is treated like a גוי, so he cannot. That is the case of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say.' It introduces a second, alternative answer.
'It is not difficult.' The two sources speak about different cases.
Someone who habitually breaks שבת.
In private, secretly.
In public, openly.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the rule that someone who openly breaks שבת is treated like a גוי for עירובין.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. Breaking שבת in private: he CAN give up his rights (the משנה). Breaking שבת in public: he CANNOT, because he is like a גוי (the ברייתא).

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it is not difficult:
here, it refers to an apostate who desecrates Shabbat in private,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case, where giving up his rights does work.

phrases.english: there, it refers to an apostate who desecrates Shabbat in public.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case, where he's treated like a גוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 8 that keeps the text unchanged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak about the same kind of צדוקי, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about a private שבת-breaker, whose giving up of rights is valid. The ברייתא speaks about a public שבת-breaker, who is like a גוי.

steps.title: Which תנא matches the ברייתא about a מומר and גילוי פנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: 'A מומר and a גילוי פנים cannot give up his rights.' It asks whose opinion this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow: 'A מומר and a brazen-faced person cannot give up his rights'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. First it checks the ברייתא's wording (Steps 12–13), and then it answers in Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know some opinions treat a public שבת-breaker like a גוי, the גמרא wants to place this ברייתא with the right opinion. But the phrase 'מומר and גילוי פנים' is odd, and the next step points that out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose opinion does it follow?'
'Which was taught' in a ברייתא.
Brazen-faced. Someone who openly and shamelessly goes against the Torah.
Gives up his rights in the alleyway so the others may carry.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught:
An apostate and a brazen-faced person
he does not renounce his rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the public/private distinction of Step 10 to identify the author of another ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a מומר or גילוי פנים cannot give up his rights.

steps.title: Isn't a brazen-faced person already a מומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא lists 'מומר' and 'גילוי פנים' separately. Someone who openly defies the Torah is a מומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A brazen-faced person, isn't he a מומר?
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering whose opinion it is, the גמרא questions the ברייתא's wording. It says the two items listed seem to be the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who shamelessly defies the Torah is exactly what a מומר is. So listing them as two separate items makes no sense, and the wording needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is he?' Here it means: isn't he already that?

phrases.english: A brazen-faced person — is he not an apostate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pauses the question of Step 11 to challenge the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of 'מומר' and 'גילוי פנים' as two separate categories.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A brazen-faced Torah violator is by definition a מומר, so the list repeats itself.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: a מומר who acts brazenly
steps.stepSummary: Read the ברייתא as 'מומר בגילוי פנים', meaning a מומר who sins openly. Such a person cannot give up his rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: a מומר who acts brazenly cannot give up his rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. It is not two people. It is one kind of person: a מומר who sins openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בגילוי פנים' describes the מומר. It means he is a public sinner. This links the ברייתא to the 'בפרהסיא' case from Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' It introduces a corrected reading.
A מומר who sins openly, meaning a public violator.
He is not able to give up his rights. It does not work.

phrases.english: Rather: an apostate who is brazen-faced —
phrases.notes: One person who sins publicly, not two separate people.

phrases.english: cannot renounce his rights,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate categories, a מומר and a brazen-faced person.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one category: a מומר who sins openly cannot give up his rights.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Now that the wording is fixed, the גמרא answers the question of Step 11: this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is it? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers its question. The ruling that a public מומר cannot give up his rights matches רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 we saw that, according to the ברייתא, רבי יהודה treats the public שבת-breaking צדוקי like a גוי. The fixed ברייתא says the same thing about a public מומר. So it fits רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the opinion of רבי יהודה.

steps.whatToRemember: A מומר who breaks שבת in private can still give up his rights in an alleyway. A מומר who breaks שבת in public is treated like a גוי and cannot. This is רבי יהודה's view, and the ברייתא of 'מומר בגילוי פנים' follows it.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the wording fixed in Step 13, answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who treats a public שבת-breaker like a גוי.

steps.title: The man who hid his ring from רבי יהודה נשיאה
steps.stepSummary: A man carried a coral ring on שבת. When he saw רבי יהודה נשיאה, he covered it. רבי יהודה נשיאה ruled that such a person can give up his rights according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who went out on שבת wearing a coral ring. When he saw רבי יהודה נשיאה, he covered it. רבי יהודה נשיאה said: Someone like this can give up his rights in the courtyard, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that shows the rule from Step 10 in action. Someone who breaks שבת but hides it is not a public violator, so his ביטול רשות works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man broke שבת by carrying the ring into the public domain. But he hid it out of shame, which shows he was not sinning openly. Earlier the ברייתא was fixed to read 'מומר בגילוי פנים' (Step 13). Since this man was not sinning בגילוי פנים, רבי יהודה would allow him to give up his rights.

keyTerms.meaning: A coral ring (or bead); carrying it out on שבת was forbidden
He covered it (hid it)
Gives up his rights in the shared courtyard, so others may carry there
The נשיא (head of the Jewish community) in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רבי יהודה here. רבי יהודה נשיאה is the one who saw the man and gave the ruling. The 'רבי יהודה' in his words is the earlier תנא whose opinion the ברייתא follows (Step 14).
steps.whyThisMatters: Hiding a sin shows the person still respects the Torah. That is what keeps him in the 'private violator' category instead of the 'public violator' category.

phrases.english: A certain man went out with a coral ring.
phrases.notes: On שבת, into the public domain, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: When he saw Rabbi Yehuda Nesia,
he covered it.
phrases.notes: He did not want the sage to see his violation.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Yehuda Nesia) said: Someone like this
can give up his rights, according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He is a private violator, not a מומר בגילוי פנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the conclusion of Steps 13–14 with a real case: a hidden violator may give up his rights according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between a public and a private שבת violator for ביטול רשות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man who hid his coral ring from רבי יהודה נשיאה

steps.title: רב הונא defines a ישראל מומר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that a ישראל מומר is someone who desecrates שבת in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Who is a Jew who is a מומר? Someone who breaks שבת in public.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב הונא gives a definition of who counts as a ישראל מומר. It connects to the topic of public שבת violators.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא makes public שבת desecration the test for being a מומר. This implies that other sins, or sinning in private, do not make someone a מומר. The next step will ask what source this definition is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who has broken away from Torah observance
One who desecrates שבת
In public, openly

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Who is an apostate Jew?
This is one who desecrates Shabbat in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אֵיזֶהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the theme of public violators and offers a general definition of a מומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל מומר is one who desecrates שבת in public.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks whose view this is, starting with רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks which opinion רב הונא follows. If he follows רבי מאיר, who says one who is suspect in one matter is suspect in the whole Torah, then even one ordinary sin should make someone a מומר, not only שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Whose opinion is this? If it follows רבי מאיר, who said that one who is suspect in one matter is suspect in the entire Torah, then even sinning in any one of the Torah's prohibitions should be enough too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's definition with a two-sided question. Here is the first side: according to רבי מאיר, the definition is too narrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a person suspected of one sin is suspected of all sins. If so, any single sin should be enough to make someone a מומר. Why would רב הונא need public שבת desecration specifically?

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose opinion is this?)
Suspected of (violating) one matter
Suspected of (violating) the entire Torah
Prohibitions

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him: According to whom?
If according to Rabbi Meir, who said:
One suspected of one matter
is suspected of the entire Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶחָד מִכׇּל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נָמֵי.
phrases.english: then even with one of any of the Torah's prohibitions as well (he should be a מומר).
phrases.notes: Not only שבת: any single sin would be enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: כְּמַאן? אִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's definition from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's limiting the definition of a מומר to public שבת desecration
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי מאיר, one sin makes a person suspect for everything. So any one prohibition, not specifically public שבת desecration, should define a מומר.

steps.title: The second side: according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן begins the second side of his question. The רבנן hold that one who is suspect in one matter is not suspect in the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows the רבנן, didn't they say: One who is suspect in one matter is not suspect in the entire Torah,
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts the other side of his challenge, according to the רבנן. This line is setting up the next move, and the full punch line continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר. They hold that a sin in one area does not make a person suspect in other areas. This seems to clash with calling someone a full מומר just because of one kind of sin, even שבת. The exact conclusion of this side comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view, against רבי מאיר)
But didn't they say?
Is not

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished yet. Don't try to conclude the challenge from these words alone; the גמרא completes it in the next lines.

phrases.english: If according to the Rabbis, didn't they say:
One suspected of one matter

phrases.aramaic: לָא הָוֵי חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: is not suspected of the entire Torah,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second side of רב נחמן's two-sided challenge begun in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's definition of a מומר, examined according to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן say a sin in one area does not make someone suspect in all areas. The full objection is completed in the following lines.
